minutes.headline: Committee moved two small transfers, declared an old sedan surplus, and backed a collaborative capital reserve fund.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with presentations from the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Professional Development Committee. The superintendent reported on the Student Opportunity Act, after-school care and community events. The committee took routine votes on transfers, minutes, a surplus vehicle, a collaborative reserve fund and a donation. Public comment covered an opioid forum and a parent's privacy question on mental health screening.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to accept two small budget transfers: one from electricity to fuel oil for emergency generators, one from extended day to the town for classroom rental.
The committee voted to declare a 2006 Pontiac G6 sedan excess and offer it for sale.
The committee voted to accept a collaborative capital reserve fund, so excess collaborative money would go to van replacement rather than back to districts.
The outdoor facilities signage draft was sent out for coordination again and will return for action at the next meeting.
The committee agreed to revisit its school funding resolution and send it to legislators and the governor.

why_it_matters: The extended day rental charge rose with the fifth classroom, and the transfers show how small account moves cover building costs in the school budget, which taxes mostly fund.
The collaborative reserve changes where unspent collaborative money goes: into a vehicle replacement fund instead of back to member districts' budgets.
The Student Opportunity Act could change state aid for health insurance, special education and circuit breaker costs, but its effect on Lunenburg was not yet known.
